summary.description: One or two sentences: what the file is and what it holds.

paragraphs.description: The narrative, one topic per paragraph (contents, channels, optics, timing, what is unusual).

suggested_commands.description: Shell commands tailored to this file, most useful first.

caveats.description: Things the reader should not take for granted (reader notes, missing calibration, ...).

answers.description: Answers to the question asked with `--ask`, one per topic it touches; empty without one.

assurance.description:
Whether the file lies inside what its reader has been validated on (as `info` →
`assurance`); its summary is also the first caveat when the file is not validated.

Answer.description: One answer to an `--ask` question, from the experiment model.

answer.description: The answer in one or two sentences; says so when the file does not record it.

fields.description: Paths of the fields the answer came from (into the `info` JSON, or `experiment.*`).

Assurance.description: The per-file assurance block of `info` (every view) and `check`.

summary.description: One line for people and agents.

fingerprint.description: The variant fingerprint: `format_id` then `kind=value` for each feature, sorted.

variant.description: Each feature with its corpus evidence.

reasons.description: Why the level is not `validated`, one reason per line.

calibrations.description: Vendor calibrations and corrections the file carries, and whether they were applied.

inferred_fields.description: Normalized fields whose meaning is inferred rather than specified.

inferred.description: Values derived by a rule instead of read, with the evidence for each rule.

strict_refuses.description: Outputs `--strict` (MCP `strict: true`) refuses to return for this file.

strict_withholds.description:
Fields `--strict` withholds (returned as null; asking for one with `--only` exits 6)
while the rest of the output is returned.

reader_confidence.description: The reader's overall confidence (evidence rubric), for context.

AssuranceLevel.description: How far a file lies inside what its reader has been validated on.

oneOf.description:
Every variant feature was read correctly on development files confirmed by an
independent reader; nothing undecoded, assumed or left uncalibrated.

Values are decoded along validated paths, but something is less certain: a descriptive
feature (writer version, instrument) never seen, a feature seen only without an
independent reader, a structure left out, or a value assumed.

Some output depends on a variant never validated (or on an undecoded structure or an
unapplied calibration): its values may be wrong. `strict_refuses` lists those outputs.

VariantFeature.description: One feature of the file's fingerprint, with the corpus evidence for it.

scope.description: Outputs whose decoding depends on it (empty: descriptive only).

corpus_files.description: Development-corpus files with this value confirmed by an independent reader.

oneOf.description: The container or format version stored in the file.
The software (or library) that wrote the file.
The writer's version, usually reduced to major.minor.
The instrument model or family that acquired the data.
Compression or encoding of the stored samples.
How samples are stored: pixel type, samples per pixel and their order, value width.
Structural layout: pyramids, mosaics, multi-file sets, directory layouts, loops.
Acquisition mode (DDA, SRM, profile/centroid, episodic, 2-D NMR, kinetic read, ...).
Dialect of a text or spreadsheet export.
A kind of record or block present in the file.

A normalized field the file has, among those tracked for oracle coverage
([`TRACKED_FIELDS`]): validated when development files' oracle comparisons checked it.

A rule by which a normalized value was derived rather than read
(`tables[].extra.reads[].mode by detector code`): validated when development files'
oracle comparisons checked the field it derives.

Scope.description: Which outputs of a file a feature, a structure or a calibration affects.

oneOf.description: The normalized metadata (`info`, all its views): sizes, channels, instrument, times.
Image planes (`planes`, `stats`, `export` of images, `preview`).
Mass spectra and scan headers (`scans`, `spectrum`, `analyze chromatogram`, mzML export).
Sampled signals (`trace`, electrophysiology, chromatograms, NMR and IR/Raman spectra).
Tables (FCS events, plate reads, qPCR results, event and peak tables).

FeatureStatus.description: How the corpus covers one feature value.

oneOf.description: Development files with this value match an independent reader.
Development files with this value were read, but no independent reader confirms them.
No development file has this value.

Undecoded.description: A structure the reader met in the file but did not decode.

structure.description: What the structure is, in the format notes' vocabulary.

scope.description:
Outputs that may be incomplete or wrong because of it. Empty: it is left out and the
values returned do not depend on it.

detail.description: What is known about it and what the reader does instead.

Assumed.description: A value the reader assumed (a default, a guess from context) instead of reading it.

field.description: JSON path of the value in `info` (e.g. `traces[0].channels[1].unit`).

detail.description: Why it was assumed and from what.

Calibration.description: A vendor calibration or correction the file carries.

name.description: What it calibrates (`m/z (MzCalibration)`, `ADC to µV`, `spillover compensation`).

status.description: Applied, not applied, or available on request.

detail.description: How it is (or is not) applied and how to get calibrated values.

CalibrationStatus.description: Whether a vendor calibration or correction stored in the file was applied.

oneOf.description: Applied: returned values are calibrated as the vendor software shows them.
Not applied: returned values differ from what the vendor software reports.

Carried by the file, applied only on request or by downstream analysis (the vendor's
raw view does not apply it either), e.g. FCS compensation or a flat-field profile.

InferredFields.description:
Fields whose meaning was inferred (reverse-engineered from corpus files), not read from a
specification: the `inferred` entries of the reader's provenance map.

count.description: How many normalized fields have inferred meaning.

of.description: How many normalized fields carry provenance at all.

examples.description: Up to 12 of their JSON paths (`info --view full` → `provenance` has all).

InferredValue.description: A value derived by a rule, with the corpus evidence for the rule.

field.description: JSON path of the value in `info`.

status.description: `validated` when development files' oracles confirmed values derived by this rule.

Withheld.description:
A field `--strict` withholds: it is present, but its value was assumed, derived by a rule no
independent reader confirmed, or never compared with an independent reader.

field.description: JSON path pattern in `info` (`[]` matches any index).

Confidence.description: Per-format confidence summary shown by `info` and `self formats`.

oneOf.description: Validated against an oracle across the corpus; structure from vendor docs or a spec.
Validated on the corpus; some fields inferred.
Early support; expect gaps.
